title: Korean Jin
capsule: Jin (辰) was a confederacy of chiefdoms occupying the southern part of the Korean peninsula during the late Iron Age, attested in Chinese Han-dynasty sources including the Hou Hanshu and the Sanguozhi (Weizhi section). Divided into the Mahan, Jinhan, and Byeonhan confederacies, Jin formed the matrix from which the Three Kingdoms of Korea (Baekje, Silla, Gaya) would later crystallize; the term 'Jin' as a unified political entity probably refers to an earlier stage of coalescence before these successor polities differentiated. Its ruler bore the title of Mahan king, but real authority was highly decentralized across dozens of small chiefdoms.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Jin is known almost entirely from brief Chinese textual references and inferred from archaeology; its territorial extent and internal structure are poorly attested and reconstructions remain substantially speculative.
